title: Prefer the packaging expansion for the conservative monetization choice

problem_spec.request: Recommend the best monetization strategy for a prosumer product moving upmarket into teams without killing the simplicity that made it spread initially.
constraints: Maintain a credible self-serve entry point.
Do not depend on enterprise procurement for the next 12 months.
success_criteria: Preserve organic adoption and avoid pricing confusion.

objective.name: conservative_option
objective.description: Choose the safer monetization move that can raise team revenue without undermining self-serve adoption.

candidate.thesis: Introduce a team workspace bundle above the self-serve core
candidate.mechanism: Keep the individual self-serve plan intact, then sell teams a clearer bundle with shared workspaces, approval controls, and admin reporting that compounds existing usage instead of hiding the core behind a paywall.
assumptions: Teams will pay more for collaboration and control once the individual workflow already proves value.
failure_modes: May leave some upside on the table if team willingness to pay is higher than expected.
unknowns: Which bundle line items matter most to the first team buyers?
candidate.implementation_shape: Launch one higher-priced team tier with clear collaboration value and simple upgrade messaging.
evidence: The brief wants more revenue per active team without pricing confusion.

hidden_dependencies: Requires strong messaging so the team bundle feels additive rather than punitive.
kill_shots: Fails if the collaboration features are too weak to justify the step-up.
sharp_edges: Could plateau if the team tier is underpriced.
critique.summary: The package is safe and clear, but its upside ceiling depends on strong team feature value.

candidate.thesis: Launch benchmark-backed outcome pricing for team plans
candidate.mechanism: Charge teams based on measurable workflow outcomes and include benchmark comparisons that prove the product's impact, creating a larger price envelope when the product materially improves team performance.
assumptions: Teams will trust benchmark-backed pricing and accept more variable spend in exchange for clearer ROI.
strengths: Could unlock a much larger willingness to pay if the ROI story lands.
failure_modes: Outcome pricing can confuse buyers and create trust risk early.
unknowns: Which benchmark signal is credible enough to anchor the pricing model?
candidate.implementation_shape: Pilot variable pricing with a narrow set of benchmark-backed enterprise-style cohorts.
evidence: The business wants higher team revenue, but the brief also warns against harming organic adoption.

hidden_dependencies: Needs trusted benchmarks and a pricing story that self-serve buyers can understand.
kill_shots: Can damage adoption if users see the pricing as unpredictable or manipulative.
sharp_edges: Variable pricing is hard to explain in a product-led motion.
critique.summary: The model is bold, but it adds pricing complexity and trust risk early.

expected_assessment.summary: The team workspace bundle is the safer option because it increases team revenue through clearer packaging while preserving the self-serve entry point and minimizing pricing confusion.
decisive_advantages: Higher tractability and plausibility in a product-led motion.
Lower risk of damaging organic adoption with complex pricing.
decisive_risks: May not capture the full long-term revenue ceiling.
